title: Idempotent Receiver

validation.research: Seven primary sources: Hohpe and Woolf’s Idempotent Receiver catalog entry; Chris Richardson’s Idempotent Consumer catalog entry; SQLite Transactions and UPSERT documentation; current Python sqlite3 documentation including connection context and explicit transaction control; RabbitMQ acknowledgments/publisher confirms; and Spring Integration Idempotent Receiver advice documentation. Both naturally repeatable message semantics and explicit deduplication are explained. Idempotent Consumer is an established alias. Receiver/source/logical-event scope, conflicting reuse, concurrency, acknowledgment after commit, retention, and external-effect limits are explicit. Existing Idempotent Writes remains a broader destination-focused pattern, preserving its canonical ID and Data Engineering collection; the new article focuses on the endpoint behavior and acknowledgment contract.

runnable_example.verification: Exact demo output; committed-state replay after connection reopening; legitimate new event and source scopes; conflicting SKU/quantity reuse with unchanged state; stock-constraint rollback of ledger and inventory followed by a successful retry; two simultaneous independent SQLite connections applying one effect; abrupt subprocess exit before commit with clean recovery; busy BEGIN and commit-failure propagation/rollback followed by retry; 1/1000-unit boundaries and malformed/Boolean/range rejection; ASCII identifier grammar and 64/65-character limits; idle-connection precondition without rolling back a caller-owned transaction. No broker, external-effect, or power-loss guarantee is inferred.

example_limits: Original file-backed SQLite stock receipt endpoint. A stable stock-receipts consumer, authorized source, and logical event ID form the processed key; stored SKU and units detect conflicting reuse. ASCII identifiers are 1..64 characters; each receipt carries 1..1000 physical units and stock has a 1000000-unit per-SKU constraint. BEGIN IMMEDIATE serializes writers before lookup. Processed identity/payload and stock increment share one transaction; return statuses occur only after commit. Caller owns initially idle dedicated connections and closes them; initialization failure closes before propagation. Reopening demonstrates replay after lost acknowledgment, and E902 remains distinct from E901 despite identical contents. The incrementing UPSERT alone is not idempotent. No broker, external effects, source authentication, ledger cleanup, multi-destination atomicity, automatic retry, or power-loss testing. The temporary demo directory is removed at the end. Existing Idempotent Writes remains a broader destination-focused article and is linked, not duplicated or rehomed.
